title: Degree bound is monotone
statement: Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$, and recall that $f$ has degree $\le d$ when all of its $(d{+}1)$-fold multiplicative derivatives vanish, i.e. the Gowers product $\mathrm{GP}(f, d{+}1, x, h_1,\ldots,h_{d+1}) = 1$ for every base point $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ and all directions $h_1,\ldots,h_{d+1} \in \{0,1\}^n$. If $f$ has degree $\le d$, then $f$ also has degree $\le d+1$; that is, $\mathrm{GP}(f, d{+}2, x, h_1,\ldots,h_{d+2}) = 1$ for every $x$ and all directions $h_1,\ldots,h_{d+2} \in \{0,1\}^n$.
hypotheses_covered: f has degree ≤ d: every (d+1)-fold Gowers product of f equals 1
replaced: If $f$ has degree $\le d$, then $f$ also has degree $\le d+1$.
